events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 8 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The ride was an instant (on-demand) booking cancelled by the rider 3 min 05 s after matching (accepted 17:12:00, cancelled 17:15:05), so the only route to a $6.61 cancellation fee is NS-0's rider branch, i.e. NS-4, which charges only for cancellations made after 3 minutes of matching. [F2 F5] [NS-0 NS-4]
C2: Even read under the driver-side no-show test the fee cannot stand: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so NS-1(i) fails. [F4] [NS-0 NS-1]
C3: NS-1(ii) also fails: the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 2,185 m at 17:15:05 — he never entered the 200 m arrival zone, let alone waited there. [F1 F3] [NS-1]
C4: NS-1(iii) fails as well: with no arrival at the pickup point there can be no wait of more than 3 minutes at the pickup point before cancellation, so none of NS-1's three cumulative conditions is met and NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full. [F1 F2 F3 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C5: The system records refute any suggestion that the rider cancelled a ride that was effectively already at the pickup point: the driver's own message at 17:13 estimated "About 5 min", which would put him arriving around 17:18, i.e. after the rider's 17:15:05 cancellation — and statements always lose to gps/timeline records. [F1 F2 F3 F8 F9] [NS-2]
C6: The driver's plea of traffic does not create a legitimate cancellation fee against the rider: only a minor speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) is recorded, there are no traffic incidents near the route, and weather was fair — in any case nothing in NS-1 conditions a rider-borne fee on traffic. [F10 F11 F12] [NS-1 NS-2]
C7: No alternative ground for the charge exists: no surge applied (1.0x) and the only fare item at issue is the $6.61 cancellation fee, so the refund is the full $6.61 computable from fare fact F5. [F5 F6] [NS-2 NS-4]
C8: A flag_account is warranted against the driver: his profile shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days over 900 trips, and this case would add a third default of the arrival/I'm-Here preconditions to the pattern of avoiding completion of accepted rides (account action only, not the basis of the refund). [F4 F14] [NS-2 NS-3 RD-6]
Weaknesses: The strongest point against us is the rider's own conduct: the cancellation came at 17:15:05, 3 min 5 s after matching (F2), which literally satisfies the '> 3 minutes' limb of NS-4, and the driver could argue he had accepted the job and was on his way (F9). | Ryde has no published rule letting a rider cancel free because the driver is late (NS-8 is informational and not citable), so the rider's stated reason for cancelling gains no clause support; the driver will lean on F2 and F9. | The driver's traffic excuse is at least weakly supported by a recorded speed band on Sim Avenue East (F10, band 3), which he may cite to argue the ETA was reasonable, though F11 shows no incident on the route. | The rider's own rating is 4.4 with no dispute history (F13), which cuts both ways: it shows good faith but also that we have no corroborating pattern of driver-side fee abuse to point to.
Asks: refund_full $6.61

events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Conceded on the bare timing: the cancellation at 17:15:05 was 3 min 5 s after the 17:12:00 acceptance (F2), which satisfies the 'more than 3 minutes after matching' limb that NS-4 uses to make a rider cancellation chargeable, and the record shows the $6.61 was charged (F5). We therefore do not dispute the trigger; our case rests on the fact that the fee cannot be sustained as a no-show charge and on the NS-7 remedy, not on the clock. [F2 F5] [NS-4]

[F10 F11 F12] [NS-1 NS-2 RD-4]

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
This is an instant (on-demand) RydeX booking cancelled by the rider, so NS-0 routes the case to the rider branch and to NS-4 only [F2][NS-0][NS-4]. The rider cancelled at 17:15:05, 3 min 5 s (185 s) after the 17:12:00 acceptance, i.e. more than 3 minutes after matching, and the $6.61 cancellation fee is on record [F2][F5][NS-4]. Under NS-4 that timing makes the fee chargeable and gives no refund: "All cancellations made within 3 minutes of matching are not chargeable" is the only carve-out, and 185 s exceeds it [F2][NS-4]. The trace's NS-0 and NS-4 elements check out, and the only allowed outcome is no_action.

The rider's case rests on the driver-side no-show route. NS-1's three cumulative conditions (I'm Here pressed; GPS within the pickup zone; > 3 min waited there) are each unmet: driver_pressed_here_at is null and driver_arrived_at is null [F3][F4][NS-1]. But NS-1 and NS-2 are the driver-cancels branch of NS-0, and here the rider cancelled [F2][NS-0]. NS-2's full refund therefore cannot be triggered on this record [F2][NS-2]. Critically, this also means no account action is available: NS-2's flag attaches only where the driver taps I'm Here while GPS shows him outside the pickup zone, which did not occur [F3][F4][NS-2].

The GPS record is adverse to the driver's position — closest approach 2,185 m at the moment of cancellation, never within 200 m [F1][NS-1] — and the driver's own chat estimate of "about 5 min" at 17:13 would put arrival after the cancellation [F8][F9][NS-4]. But these facts rebut a no-show claim the driver has not made; they do not create a clause ground to waive an NS-4 fee, because Ryde publishes no free-cancellation right for a late driver and NS-8 is informational and not citable [F1][F2][F9][NS-4]. The traffic record (Sims Avenue East band 3, no incidents, fair weather) is equally immaterial to a rider-borne NS-4 fee and, being band 3, would not meet RD-4(b) in any event [F10][F11][F12][RD-4].

No surplus item exists to refund: surge is 1.0× and the only fee in issue is the published $6.61 cancellation fee, so there is no unpublished add-on to strip out under FARE-1 [F5][F6][FARE-1]. The rider's clean profile and the driver's two upheld no-show disputes do not decide this case — profile facts cannot carry a finding on their own, and RD-6's flag requires the case against the driver to be made out, which on a rider-cancellation record it is not [F13][F14][RD-6]. Amount is left null because no money moves under no_action.

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; no refund voucher to issue. Record that no driver-fault or arrival-button breach is found here, so no account action against the driver. Optionally relay to the rider (via RydeHELP) that driver-lateness is not a free-cancellation ground under the published policy and that a goodwill waiver is at Ryde's discretion under NS-7.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We looked at your cancellation and the fee stands. You cancelled just over three minutes after a driver was matched, and the $6.61 cancellation fee applies from three minutes onward under our published policy. Being late is not a free-cancellation ground, though Ryde can waive a fee as a goodwill gesture at its discretion. So no refund or voucher is being issued. Nothing changes on your account and no further action is needed from you.

DRIVER: No action against you. The booking was cancelled by the rider just over three minutes after matching, so the cancellation fee applies to the rider, and we found no failure on your side. No account action or review is being taken. You do not need to do anything.

ruling.reasoning:
This is an instant (on-demand) RydeX booking cancelled by the rider, so NS-0 routes the case to the rider branch and to NS-4 only [F2][NS-0][NS-4]. The rider cancelled at 17:15:05, 3 min 5 s (185 s) after the 17:12:00 acceptance, i.e. more than 3 minutes after matching, and the $6.61 cancellation fee is on record [F2][F5][NS-4]. Under NS-4 that timing makes the fee chargeable and gives no refund: "All cancellations made within 3 minutes of matching are not chargeable" is the only carve-out, and 185 s exceeds it [F2][NS-4]. The trace's NS-0 and NS-4 elements check out, and the only allowed outcome is no_action.

The rider's case rests on the driver-side no-show route. NS-1's three cumulative conditions (I'm Here pressed; GPS within the pickup zone; > 3 min waited there) are each unmet: driver_pressed_here_at is null and driver_arrived_at is null [F3][F4][NS-1]. But NS-1 and NS-2 are the driver-cancels branch of NS-0, and here the rider cancelled [F2][NS-0]. NS-2's full refund therefore cannot be triggered on this record [F2][NS-2]. Critically, this also means no account action is available: NS-2's flag attaches only where the driver taps I'm Here while GPS shows him outside the pickup zone, which did not occur [F3][F4][NS-2].

The GPS record is adverse to the driver's position — closest approach 2,185 m at the moment of cancellation, never within 200 m [F1][NS-1] — and the driver's own chat estimate of "about 5 min" at 17:13 would put arrival after the cancellation [F8][F9][NS-4]. But these facts rebut a no-show claim the driver has not made; they do not create a clause ground to waive an NS-4 fee, because Ryde publishes no free-cancellation right for a late driver and NS-8 is informational and not citable [F1][F2][F9][NS-4]. The traffic record (Sims Avenue East band 3, no incidents, fair weather) is equally immaterial to a rider-borne NS-4 fee and, being band 3, would not meet RD-4(b) in any event [F10][F11][F12][RD-4].

No surplus item exists to refund: surge is 1.0× and the only fee in issue is the published $6.61 cancellation fee, so there is no unpublished add-on to strip out under FARE-1 [F5][F6][FARE-1]. The rider's clean profile and the driver's two upheld no-show disputes do not decide this case — profile facts cannot carry a finding on their own, and RD-6's flag requires the case against the driver to be made out, which on a rider-cancellation record it is not [F13][F14][RD-6]. Amount is left null because no money moves under no_action.

certificate: ✓ NS-4 rider cancelled more than 3 min after matching [case] 185 s after acceptance (F2)

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The ride was an instant (on-demand) booking cancelled by the rider 3 min 05 s after matching (accepted 17:12:00, cancelled 17:15:05), so the only route to a $6.61 cancellation fee is NS-0's rider branch, i.e. NS-4, which charges only for cancellations made after 3 minutes of matching.
Even read under the driver-side no-show test the fee cannot stand: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so NS-1(i) fails.

NS-1(ii) also fails: the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 2,185 m at 17:15:05 — he never entered the 200 m arrival zone, let alone waited there.

NS-1(iii) fails as well: with no arrival at the pickup point there can be no wait of more than 3 minutes at the pickup point before cancellation, so none of NS-1's three cumulative conditions is met and NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full.

The system records refute any suggestion that the rider cancelled a ride that was effectively already at the pickup point: the driver's own message at 17:13 estimated "About 5 min", which would put him arriving around 17:18, i.e. after the rider's 17:15:05 cancellation — and statements always lose to gps/timeline records.

The driver's plea of traffic does not create a legitimate cancellation fee against the rider: only a minor speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) is recorded, there are no traffic incidents near the route, and weather was fair — in any case nothing in NS-1 conditions a rider-borne fee on traffic.
No alternative ground for the charge exists: no surge applied (1.0x) and the only fare item at issue is the $6.61 cancellation fee, so the refund is the full $6.61 computable from fare fact F5.

A flag_account is warranted against the driver: his profile shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days over 900 trips, and this case would add a third default of the arrival/I'm-Here preconditions to the pattern of avoiding completion of accepted rides (account action only, not the basis of the refund).

weaknesses: The strongest point against us is the rider's own conduct: the cancellation came at 17:15:05, 3 min 5 s after matching (F2), which literally satisfies the '> 3 minutes' limb of NS-4, and the driver could argue he had accepted the job and was on his way (F9).

Ryde has no published rule letting a rider cancel free because the driver is late (NS-8 is informational and not citable), so the rider's stated reason for cancelling gains no clause support; the driver will lean on F2 and F9.

The driver's traffic excuse is at least weakly supported by a recorded speed band on Sim Avenue East (F10, band 3), which he may cite to argue the ETA was reasonable, though F11 shows no incident on the route.
The rider's own rating is 4.4 with no dispute history (F13), which cuts both ways: it shows good faith but also that we have no corroborating pattern of driver-side fee abuse to point to.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance (17:12:00 → 17:15:05), i.e. more than 3 minutes after matching, so under the published cancellation rule the $6.61 fee is chargeable and no refund is due.

This is a rider-side cancellation, so the only route to a fee is NS-4, and NS-4 makes the fee valid for any cancellation made after 3:00 from matching; the driver's distance or ETA is not a ground for a free cancellation under the policy.

The driver never pressed "I'm Here" and was never recorded at the pickup point, so none of the driver-fault branches (NS-1 / NS-2 / NS-3) apply and no fee-waiver or account flag can be built against the driver on this record.

The driver's own chat estimate was about 5 minutes in "traffic", and LTA speed-band data shows SIMS AVENUE EAST at band 3 (20–29 km/h) during 17:07–17:20 — slow but not severe (band 1 or 2) — with no incidents recorded, so the driver's delay is explained by ordinary traffic rather than any fault of his.

The rider's own profile shows 0 disputes in 90 days, so there is no evidence of a pattern of abusive rider behaviour, but equally nothing in the record shows the driver acted improperly; the $6.61 was charged under the published policy and should stand.

weaknesses: F1 (gps) shows the driver's closest approach was 2185 m at the very moment of cancellation and that he never entered the 200 m pickup radius — the rider will argue he was far away and that NS-4's fee is unfair in practice, even though NS-4 permits it.
F4 (timeline) shows no "I'm Here" press and F3 shows no recorded arrival, so the driver cannot claim the rider no-showed and cannot claim the $4.50 driver share of the fee under NS-1.

F14 (profile) shows the driver already has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days; if the rider frames this as a repeated pattern, the judge may attach flag_account as an additional action even though it is not the main finding.

F8 (chat) shows the driver told the rider "about 5 min" at 17:13, which is later than the 3:05 the rider waited; the rider will use this to argue she cancelled within the driver's own promised window and should not be charged.

points.response: Conceded on the bare timing: the cancellation at 17:15:05 was 3 min 5 s after the 17:12:00 acceptance (F2), which satisfies the 'more than 3 minutes after matching' limb that NS-4 uses to make a rider cancellation chargeable, and the record shows the $6.61 was charged (F5). We therefore do not dispute the trigger; our case rests on the fact that the fee cannot be sustained as a no-show charge and on the NS-7 remedy, not on the clock.

NS-4's timing limb makes a fee chargeable but does not entitle the driver, who never entered the pickup zone (F1: closest approach 2,185 m at the very moment of cancellation; F3: driver_arrived_at null), to keep a fee premised on the rider having failed to show at a car that was never there; the policy's own remedy for a rider who disputes such a fee is the NS-7 fee-waiver request, which the rider has made within 30 days.

We agree no driver-fault branch is triggered on this record, but D3 is beside our point: the rider was charged $6.61 (F5) even though the driver never pressed 'I'm Here' (F4) and never came within the pickup radius (F1), so the charge cannot be justified as a no-show fee and NS-2 directs the $6.61 refunded in full rather than the fee standing.

Band 3 at 20-29 km/h is not severe congestion under the data layer, and there were no incidents near the route with fair weather (F10, F11, F12) — but traffic is irrelevant here because NS-1 and NS-2 turn on arrival and the 'I'm Here' press, and the closure of the driver-fault branch is exactly why a no-show-based retention of the fee fails; RD-4 governs route deviation, not cancellation fees.

The rider's clean 90-day record (F13: 1,495-day account, 0 disputes) shows a first-time, good-faith cancellation, whereas the driver's own record shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F14), so a flag_account is warranted against the driver while the contested $6.61 — the only fare item in issue, no surge (F5, F6) — is refunded.

Conceded as to the mechanics: this was an instant ride cancelled by the rider at 17:15:05, and NS-4 governs. But that runs against the rider — NS-4 charges exactly this case, because the cancellation came after 3 minutes of matching (F2), so C1's own clause validates the $6.61 rather than voiding it.

C2 is true but inert: NS-1's conditions only matter when the driver cancels and claims a rider no-show under NS-0, and here the rider cancelled the booking herself (F2), so the null I'm Here record (F4) has no bearing on whether the rider-triggered NS-4 fee stands.

Inert for the same reason: the 2,185 m closest approach and null arrival record (F1, F3) rebut a driver-side no-show claim, which the driver has never made — the fee arises from the rider's own cancellation, not from a driver arrival-button act.

C5 refutes a claim nobody makes: the driver does not contend the rider cancelled a ride already at the pickup point, only that she cancelled a validly accepted RydeX trip more than 3 minutes after matching (F2, F3), and the 17:13 five-minute estimate (F8) is consistent with a driver still en route — precisely the situation NS-4 prices at $6.61.

C4 inverts the structure of NS-0: NS-2's full refund operates on the driver-cancels branch, whereas here the rider cancelled (F2), a case NS-4 resolves with no refund for any cancellation after 3 minutes of matching.

C6 is right that traffic does not condition a rider-borne fee, and that cuts for the driver: NS-4 imposes the fee purely on the post-3-minute timing (F2), so neither the rider's 'driver was far away' reason nor the band-3 speed record (F10) can waive it.
The $6.61 is not an extraneous add-on: it is the published cancellation fee on record (F5), and no surge or hidden item is in issue (F6), so there is no surplus to refund under FARE-1 either.

C8 misuses the profile facts: F14 records 2 upheld disputes but no finding that any arrival or I'm Here precondition was breached in this case — here the driver never pressed I'm Here (F4) and the rider cancelled (F2), so there is no third default to add, and flag_account under RD-6 requires this case to be made out, which it is not.

Nothing changes on your account and no further action is needed from you.
